value.name: Asha and Daniel acknowledge difficulty
value.description: Asha and Daniel openly acknowledge that their relationship was difficult and that Daniel was not easy to deal with.

value.name: Daniel admits Asha handled him well
value.description: Daniel thanks Asha for handling him better than he deserved and recognizes her effort in their relationship.
evidence: "I know that. I want to say, for the record, that I know that. You handled me better than I deserved."
"I handled you as well as I could. You met me halfway. Eventually."

value.name: Asha frames their reconciliation as gradual
value.description: Asha reflects that meeting halfway usually happens eventually, implying their connection developed later than ideal but still meaningfully.
evidence: "That is when most people meet anyone halfway, Daniel. Eventually is the standard. Earlier is the exception. You came in under the standard. That is what I would say if anyone asked."

value.name: Daniel thanks Asha
value.description: Daniel smiles briefly and thanks Asha for her honesty and patience.

value.name: Asha and Daniel say good night
value.description: Asha and Daniel exchange a final good-night before parting ways.

value.name: Asha leaves the house
value.description: Asha walks down the steps and heads away from the row house along Spruce Street.
evidence: She walked down the steps and along Spruce Street toward the corner.

value.name: Asha looks back at the house
value.description: At the corner, Asha pauses and looks back at the row house, taking in the lit windows, visible fire, and the people inside.
evidence: At the corner she stopped and looked back.

The row house stood between its neighbors with its front windows lit and its fire visible behind the curtain and the small powder of snow gathering on its railings, and inside it three people were doing the dishes and talking

value.name: Asha recognizes the house as settled and beginning
value.description: Asha mentally judges the house to be legally settled yet, in a deeper sense, just beginning.
evidence: the house was, by any legal standard she could think of, settled, and by any other standard she could think of, beginning.

value.name: Asha goes home
value.description: Asha turns the corner and heads home after leaving the row house behind.
evidence: She turned the corner and went home.
